page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating up to 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture includes a generous 480 MB L3 cache and supports modern vector and matrix acceleration instructions, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). Memory configuration consists of 512 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage entirely, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage integration for system and data persistence. In benchmark evaluations, the D128s_v7 demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, reaching 132,083.9 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 123,481.9 in PassMark CPU tests. The presence of AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets drives high throughput on extended instruction suites and cryptographic workloads. Memory subsystem throughput is equally pronounced, showing top-tier performance on uncached large-block reads at 452.95 GB/sec and writes at 182.27 GB/sec.

While single-core compute performance sits in the middle 50% percentile, the sheer density of dedicated vCPUs provides exceptional aggregate throughput. The server handles 184.13 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves static web serving throughput of 179.77 GB/sec. CPU-driven inference speeds are strong for prompt processing across model parameter sizes from 135M to 70B, although text generation performance settles near median levels due to memory latency bounds inherent to CPU execution without discrete GPU acceleration.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the D128s_v7 consolidates massive parallel compute capacity into a single general-purpose footprint, eliminating the management overhead of multi-node clusters for parallel CPU tasks. Given the absence of local ephemeral storage, workloads must account for remote block storage configurations. The instance is suited for high-density web servers, large in-memory caches, distributed compilation pipelines, enterprise database hosting, and high-throughput data processing operations.

Built on x86_64 architecture with 64 physical cores, it features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, paired with a large 480 MB L3 cache. The server does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, depending on remote Premium Storage for data volumes. Performance metrics place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the top tier, demonstrating 184.13 million Redis SET operations per second and exceptional data compression throughput. While single-thread operations exhibit moderate performance, the aggregated compute power delivers strong cost efficiency for highly parallel enterprise workloads. The D128s_v7 is suited for massive in-memory databases, large-scale web serving, data transformation pipelines, and parallel enterprise application hosting.
